declared_purpose: Provide web search, retrieval, and authenticated Chromium browser interaction through a shared local CDP Proxy. Supporting features locate previously visited/internal URLs and retain reusable site knowledge. Browser selection, preservation of user tabs, cleanup of Agent tabs, and service reuse are explicit requirements; broad readiness queries, response fields, and append-only logging are implementation choices. Sources: SKILL.md:2-3,74-84,104-112,125-138,227-233,272-278.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve web information through alternative tools
data_operations.source: Agent-selected queries and URLs; target websites
data_operations.data_scope: Search terms, requested URLs, fetched HTML/content, and WebFetch extraction prompts. The entry document describes WebFetch processing by a small model.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured WebSearch/WebFetch components or curl's destination website; results return to the caller. Backend providers are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Tool selection depends on the task, page accessibility, and need for login or interaction.

data_operations.operation: Optionally disclose a target URL to a conversion service
data_operations.data_scope: Target URL and the page content converted to Markdown; no browser-cookie forwarding is specified.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Third-party service r.jina.ai; converted content returns to its caller.
data_operations.condition: Optional preprocessing, encouraged when suitable for reducing token use. Service-side collection and retention are undocumented.

data_operations.operation: Discover browsers and infer debugging availability locally
data_operations.source: Platform application-data roots and explicitly selected candidate folders
data_operations.data_scope: Top-level folder names; bounded descendant directory metadata; existence of Local State; DevToolsActivePort contents; TCP listening status. Browser identity and debugging availability are inferred from these observations.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Probe/check process memory and stdout to the caller, with browser paths and inferred status.
data_operations.condition: First-run inventory requires no browser preference and no reusable service. Candidate probing is limited to supplied folders, depth 3 and 500 directories; it does not read Local State contents.

data_operations.source: ~/.web-access/config.env, optional --browser argument, and selected browser directory
data_operations.data_scope: Configuration key/value text, WEB_ACCESS_BROWSER, optional WEB_ACCESS_CDP_PORT, normalized directory identity, and debugging endpoint. Directory validation uses filesystem metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local discovery process; selected preference persists in ~/.web-access/config.env. Temporary overrides are not written there.
data_operations.condition: Configuration is read during selection. First setup explicitly requires user selection before writing the preference; check-deps creates a missing config from a referenced template.

data_operations.operation: Copy legacy user data without deleting originals
data_operations.source: Current legacy skill data and, for the recognized plugin layout, the newest eligible sibling version
data_operations.data_scope: Legacy config.env and recursively enumerated regular site-pattern files; migration timestamp, source paths, and copy counts.
data_operations.condition: check-deps invokes migration before configuration creation. An existing marker prevents rescanning; existing destination files are not overwritten.

data_operations.operation: Maintain a shared local browser-control connection
data_operations.source: Selected browser endpoint and HTTP requests
data_operations.data_scope: CDP commands, parameters, command responses, session identifiers, managed-tab identifiers, access times, and pending-command state.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTP Proxy bound to 127.0.0.1; WebSocket to the selected browser on 127.0.0.1; transient process maps and requesting callers.
data_operations.condition: The service persists across tasks as explicitly required. Concurrent connection attempts share one connection attempt; normal command results resolve to their callers.

data_operations.operation: Return health information and perform readiness checks
data_operations.source: Proxy runtime state and browser target listing
data_operations.data_scope: Browser directory identity, debugging port, process/instance identifiers, revision and activity counters. Startup/reconnection checks additionally receive all page TargetInfo objects but only test whether the result is an array.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local HTTP caller, check-deps process, or maintenance CLI. No external disclosure is shown.
data_operations.condition: Health reads do not establish a browser connection. check-deps uses /targets while starting or reconnecting; a connected healthy service bypasses that loop.

data_operations.source: Browser targets, selected document, and its direct iframe/frame elements
data_operations.data_scope: All page TargetInfo fields for /targets; title, URL and readiness for /info; iframe IDs, URLs, id/name/src attributes and cross-process classification for /frames. The iframe helper internally obtains browser-wide target metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Proxy/helper memory and the requesting caller. Temporary remote-object groups are released.
data_operations.condition: Only when the relevant endpoint is invoked. Frame enumeration covers direct main-document frames; returned cross-process status is inferred by matching target metadata.

data_operations.operation: Navigate using the user's existing browser session
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied complete URLs and existing browser login state
data_operations.data_scope: Destination URLs, including required session-related parameters; normal browser requests to the destination. The source does not show cookie extraction by the skill.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Proxy and browser, then the requested website through browser navigation.
data_operations.condition: /new creates a background tab before navigation; /navigate and /back use a supplied target. Preserving necessary URL parameters and using existing login state are explicit requirements. Existing user tabs require an explicit user request under the entry document.

data_operations.source: Caller JavaScript, selectors or coordinates; selected page DOM
data_operations.data_scope: Serializable evaluation results; clicked element tag and up to 100 characters of text; click coordinates and interaction status. JavaScript can read/write DOM and submit forms.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browser execution context, Proxy, and requesting caller. A website receives submitted data only if the selected action triggers such a submission.
data_operations.condition: Endpoint invocation determines the action. Frame evaluation uses an isolated context sharing the frame DOM; actual expressions, form data and resulting network effects are not supplied.

data_operations.operation: Expose selected local files to a page file input
data_operations.source: Caller-provided selector and local file paths
data_operations.data_scope: Paths passed to DOM.setFileInputFiles and the corresponding browser file selection; response contains only success and file count.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local browser and selected page file input. Any subsequent upload recipient depends on page handling/submission.
data_operations.condition: Only for /setFiles. The implementation does not separately read file bytes or establish that a remote upload completed.

data_operations.operation: Capture screenshots and optionally retain media
data_operations.source: Selected page rendering, including visible video frames; extracted media URLs
data_operations.data_scope: Screenshot pixels or downloaded media. Coordinate routing also captures a low-quality viewport JPEG internally when a same-process iframe needs painting.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Explicit screenshots return binary to the caller or persist at the caller's file path. The routing screenshot stays inside the helper/CDP exchange. Public media may be downloaded locally.
data_operations.condition: Explicit screenshot/media use is task-dependent; file persistence requires the file parameter. The routing screenshot is conditional on paint being true. No screenshot-file deletion routine is shown.

data_operations.operation: Search local browser profiles, bookmarks and history
data_operations.source: Installed Chrome/Edge Local State, profile Bookmarks files, and History databases
data_operations.data_scope: Profile identifiers/names, bookmark titles, URLs and folder trails; history titles, URLs, last-visit times and visit counts. Frequency ordering derives a ranking from stored counts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local find-url process and sqlite3 subprocess; selected results go to stdout for the caller.
data_operations.condition: The entry document limits use to previously visited pages or internal systems. Implementation defaults search both browsers, every enumerated profile, both sources, and no history time bound; output defaults to 20 results per source.

data_operations.operation: Create and attempt to delete a history snapshot
data_operations.source: Each selected profile's complete History database
data_operations.data_scope: Entire database, including records outside keyword/time/result filters. Those filters apply after copying.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Temporary browser-history-*.sqlite file under os.tmpdir(), then local sqlite3.
data_operations.condition: History search uses a copy to handle the stated database-locking constraint. finally attempts unlink; deletion errors are ignored, so deletion is not guaranteed. Secure erasure is not established.

data_operations.operation: Read and persist reusable site experience
data_operations.source: Verified observations from site interaction, domain/alias metadata, and optional user-input text
data_operations.data_scope: Domain-keyed platform facts, URL patterns, selectors, strategies and dated pitfalls. check-deps lists all top-level Markdown domain filenames; match-site reads every top-level Markdown file and returns matching bodies.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.web-access/site-patterns/{domain}.md; matching content returns to the caller. No expiry or automatic deletion is specified.
data_operations.condition: Reading matching experience and writing useful verified new patterns are explicit entry requirements. match-site performs local regex matching against domain and aliases. Migration instructions require updating obsolete calls in stored experience.

data_operations.source: Proxy lifecycle, browser selection, idle cleanup and error messages
data_operations.data_scope: Absolute browser directory, port, timestamps, process/instance identifiers, closed target IDs and diagnostic text. Routine page bodies are not explicitly logged.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Append-mode os.tmpdir()/cdp-proxy.log for detached launches, receiving stdout and stderr.
data_operations.condition: check-deps opens the log when starting a detached Proxy. No rotation, expiry or log deletion is implemented in the supplied source.

data_operations.operation: Close tabs and remove transient bookkeeping
data_operations.source: Explicit target IDs and managed-tab access timestamps
data_operations.data_scope: Tabs created through /new, session entries and managed-tab entries; frame helpers separately release temporary remote objects.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browser tab state and Proxy memory.
data_operations.condition: The entry document requires closing Agent tabs at completion while preserving user tabs. Idle cleanup defaults to 15 minutes, swept every minute; shutdown closes managed tabs. Disconnect clears tracking. Tab closure does not establish deletion of browser history or site storage.

potential_excess.data_scope: All open page TargetInfo objects fetched for connection readiness
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Browser to Proxy to the local check-deps process
potential_excess.condition: Starting or reconnecting a Proxy; the loop only checks Array.isArray before reading /health.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Readiness requires a confirmed browser connection, not page inventory. This is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Trigger connection and verify connected status.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Add a connection-readiness endpoint returning status only and replace the readiness /targets calls. The inventory action is redundant for this purpose.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain shared connection attempts, browser-identity checks, authorization waiting and timeout behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: Every TargetInfo field for every open page
potential_excess.condition: A caller invokes /targets, including when it only needs Agent-created tabs or one target.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Target identification is useful, but the documented response identifies targetId, title and url; ordinary tasks should preserve existing user tabs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return enough metadata to locate the required target.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Project the documented fields and support target/managed-tab filtering. Make broader user-tab inventory explicit when needed. This narrows data in a useful listing action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep full-page discovery available for explicit user-tab tasks and attach recovery that genuinely needs it.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated browser/profile stores and ancillary bookmark/history metadata
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local find-url reads, full-history temporary snapshots, and stdout to the caller
potential_excess.condition: A URL-location task has a known browser/source or only needs title and URL, but defaults search all profiles and both browsers/sources and print folders, visit times/counts and conditional profile labels.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The supporting purpose is locating prior/internal pages. Broad defaults and ancillary output are implementation choices; visit counts are relevant for explicit frequency tasks.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Find and disambiguate the requested page.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use task-known browser/source/time restrictions first, add profile selection, and widen on failure. Make ancillary output optional when title and URL suffice.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve cross-profile fallback, necessary disambiguation, and timestamps/counts for recency or frequency requests. Query filters alone do not narrow an already copied History database.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete Bookmarks contents when no keywords were supplied
potential_excess.condition: Bookmark search is enabled without keywords.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The function explicitly returns no bookmarks for an empty-keyword query.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Move the empty-keyword check before opening/parsing Bookmarks. This removes a redundant read, rather than trimming useful results.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep keyword searches and the existing empty-query output behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: Up to 100 characters of clicked-element text
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Browser evaluation result, Proxy memory and /click or /clickAt response
potential_excess.condition: Every successful selector-based click, even when the caller only needs interaction status or coordinates.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Clicking is required for interaction; collecting element text is an additional implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Locate/click the element and report status; /clickAt also needs coordinates.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make element text optional or omit it by default while retaining status and necessary coordinates.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Allow text when needed to identify an ambiguous control or verify the intended interaction.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local match-site process memory; only matching bodies reach stdout
potential_excess.condition: Every nonempty match-site query reads every top-level Markdown file before checking its domain/aliases.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Selecting matching experience needs domain and alias metadata; unmatched bodies are not used.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Match metadata, then return matching experience.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Read/index frontmatter first and load bodies only for matches.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve domain/alias matching and invalidate any index when experience changes.

potential_excess.data_scope: Absolute browser paths, target IDs and accumulated diagnostic text
potential_excess.condition: Detached launches append to the same file; no packaged retention bound is shown.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Connection troubleshooting benefits from diagnostics; indefinite accumulation and routine absolute-path logging are implementation choices.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain enough recent status and error context to diagnose failures.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Rotate or bound logs and use browser labels instead of absolute paths for routine successful connections; expose detailed paths on diagnostic demand.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep actionable permission/configuration errors, timestamps and instance identifiers needed for maintenance.

potential_excess.data_scope: Non-experience regular files under legacy references/site-patterns/, if present
potential_excess.condition: One-time migration recursively copies every regular file except .gitkeep; it does not restrict files to the domain Markdown format.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Migration preserves configuration and reusable site experience. Runtime experience readers select top-level .md files.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Copy supported experience and any genuinely required supporting files without overwriting destination data.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Validate migration candidates against the supported experience format and explicitly include required assets instead of copying arbitrary artifacts.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain verified supporting dependencies, source precedence, non-overwrite behavior and the explicit requirement to leave originals intact.

potential_excess.data_scope: Agent-created tabs and their loaded content surviving a connection interruption
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Browser tabs after Proxy tracking is cleared
potential_excess.condition: onDisconnect clears managedTabs. If those browser tabs survive, later idle sweeps no longer know to close them.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry requires Agent-tab cleanup while keeping the shared service and user tabs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Reconnect safely and eventually close only Agent-created tabs.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Retain pending cleanup identifiers across connection loss and reconcile them against the pinned browser after reconnection.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Verify target identity before closing; never treat unrelated or replacement user tabs as managed. Actual tab survival depends on the interruption.

potential_excess.data_scope: Target URL and converted page content
potential_excess.condition: Optional conversion is chosen although direct retrieval can satisfy the task within the available content/token budget.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Jina's declared benefit is token reduction; universal retrieval also has direct alternatives. This is a conditional additional recipient, not an unconditional duplicate request.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use direct retrieval when conversion adds no necessary benefit, especially for URLs carrying session-related parameters.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep optional conversion where its compression is needed and its documented information loss does not impair the task. Preserve parameters required by the actual destination.

unknowns: WebSearch/WebFetch implementations and Jina's internal fetching, subprocessors, logging, retention and deletion are absent; downstream privacy assessment remains unresolved (SKILL.md:74-84).
The referenced templates/config.env.template is not supplied. Its literal defaults and any additional configuration fields cannot be assessed (scripts/check-deps.mjs:27,62-70).

Runtime URLs, JavaScript, selectors, files, page scripts and browser settings are unspecified. Concrete submitted data, browser-request credentials, additional network recipients and resulting website persistence cannot be determined.

Actual config, site-experience, legacy migration and browser-store contents are not supplied. Whether they contain account-specific URLs or credentials, and whether broad migration copies unrelated artifacts, remains unresolved.
History-snapshot unlink failures are ignored; actual deletion success, filesystem access controls and residual recoverability are unknown (scripts/find-url.mjs:134-165).
Closing a tab does not establish browser history/cache/site-storage deletion. Those browser behaviors and whether tabs survive a disconnect are outside the supplied implementation.
The supplied source establishes local caller returns, not subsequent caller disclosure or model-provider retention. No additional remote recipient is inferred from an ordinary tool response.
